title: Yogish Profile
content: Yogish Reddy Dwarampudi is a Cloud and DevSecOps Engineer currently working at Accenture as an Associate Software Engineer. He has 2+ years of overall professional experience at Accenture. He joined Accenture in September 2024 and initially underwent stream training in AWS Data Engineering before joining the CloudBees CI / Jenkins project in May 2025. His current professional experience focuses on enterprise CloudBees CI / Jenkins platforms, CI/CD operations, cloud infrastructure, DevSecOps, automation and platform stability. His technologies include Jenkins, CloudBees CI, AWS, Docker, Kubernetes/EKS, GitHub, Python and Bash. His current personal technical focus is expanding his Cloud and DevOps foundation into AI Engineering and Agentic AI.

title: Career Direction
content: Yogish does not consider AI a move away from Cloud and DevOps. He wants to build on his existing Cloud knowledge to create more advanced products using AI and Agentic AI. His current goal is to build systems where a user can provide a single input and an agentic system can complete the intended task with minimal manual work. His long-term goal is to become an engineer who can architect products at a high level, quickly develop an MVP, clearly communicate architecture and capabilities, evaluate security considerations and limitations, and build products capable of serving large numbers of users.

title: Education
content: Yogish completed a Bachelor of Technology in Computer Science from NBKR Institute of Science and Technology (NBKRIST), Nellore, from 2020 to 2024, with a final grade of 8.0 out of 10. He completed his MPC higher secondary education at Narayana Junior College, Nellore, from 2018 to 2020.

title: Accenture - CloudBees CI / Jenkins Platform - DevSecOps Engineer
content: Company: Accenture. Overall employment: September 2024 – Present. Role: Associate Software Engineer. After joining Accenture in September 2024, Yogish initially underwent stream training in AWS Data Engineering. He joined the CloudBees CI / Jenkins project in May 2025, where his current project experience is positioned as CloudBees CI / Jenkins Platform DevSecOps Engineer. He supports an enterprise Jenkins environment across approximately 9 lines of business, with 300+ controllers and around 3,000 builds per day. The environment includes managed controllers, Operations Center, static agents running on Windows and Linux VMs, and ephemeral agents provisioned through Kubernetes/EKS using Docker images. His work includes managing and troubleshooting Jenkins controllers, agents and CI/CD pipelines; resolving failed builds, agent connectivity issues, workspace problems and pipeline execution issues; and working with static Windows agents and WebSocket-based agent connectivity. He analyzes Jenkins logs, build failures and infrastructure issues to identify root causes and restore services. He participates in platform upgrade activities for EKS and quarterly CloudBees CI / Jenkins platform upgrades involving Operations Center, agents, plugins and managed controllers. He performs vulnerability remediation on Jenkins agents and Windows/Linux build VMs, validates and updates software where required, and performs software installations on Jenkins agents. He works with Docker base and custom images, including quarterly image updates and removal of vulnerable older versions. He supports GitHub/Jenkins CI integration, including build triggers and pipeline execution, and works with GitHub and third-party credentials such as SonarQube. He resolves Jenkins access issues and guides users through access processes. He participates in incident and problem resolution and collaborates with application, infrastructure and development teams to resolve CI/CD issues and maintain SLAs. He uses Jenkins automation jobs for operational reporting and searching build console output across controllers for specific information. He creates technical documentation and operational procedures and contributes to automation initiatives intended to reduce manual effort. The team monitors EKS workloads using Datadog and works with AWS backup and restore capabilities including Cloud Native Restore. Other operational activities include license recovery by identifying inactive users and access that can be revoked, and cleanup of inactive controllers and jobs. He uses Jira to track stories and tasks and ServiceNow for service requests and incidents. His work is performed as part of the CloudBees CI team, with senior engineers providing guidance on larger implementations.

title: Accenture Responsibilities
content: As part of the CloudBees CI / Jenkins team, Yogish supports enterprise CI/CD pipeline operations and platform stability. His responsibilities include Jenkins controller, agent and pipeline troubleshooting; failed build analysis; agent selection and connectivity troubleshooting; workspace and pipeline execution issues; static Windows/Linux agent support; WebSocket-based agent connectivity; and Kubernetes pod-agent memory troubleshooting. He analyzes Jenkins logs, build failures and infrastructure issues to identify root causes. He supports GitHub/Jenkins CI integration, including build triggers and pipeline execution, and works with credentials for GitHub and third-party services such as SonarQube. He supports Jenkins access and managed-controller access processes and guides users on access. He participates in quarterly platform upgrades involving Operations Center, agents, plugins, CJOC and managed controllers, including validation of agent connectivity and plugin versions. He participates in EKS platform upgrade activities. He carries out vulnerability remediation on Windows and Linux Jenkins agent VMs, performs required software installations, and validates software updates. He works with Docker images used by ephemeral Jenkins agents, including quarterly image updates and removal of older vulnerable versions. He monitors Kubernetes pods in EKS using Datadog and participates in AWS EKS backup and restore activities using cloud-native restore methods. He uses Jenkins automation jobs for tasks such as searching build console output across CJOC and managed controllers for specific keywords and publishing resulting data or reports. He contributes to technical documentation, operational procedures and automation initiatives that reduce manual effort. He participates in incident and problem resolution, collaborates with application, infrastructure and development teams, and helps maintain SLAs. He also works on license recovery activities by identifying inactive users whose platform access can be revoked and helps with cleanup of inactive controllers and jobs. He uses Jira to track stories and tasks and ServiceNow to work with service requests and incidents. He has supported and participated in these activities as an Associate Software Engineer, with larger implementations often handled with guidance from senior team members.

title: College Project - Grey Wolf Algorithm for Wireless Sensor Networking - Python
content: Project: Grey Wolf Algorithm for Wireless Sensor Networking. Type: B.Tech Computer Science college team project. Status: Completed. This was Yogish's final-year project. Team size: 4 students. Objective: Use the Grey Wolf Optimization algorithm to find an efficient path through wireless sensors to reach a receiver, with the goal of reducing latency and cost and improving response time. The approach can avoid inactive or damaged sensors and select an available active sensor path. Yogish's contribution: developed the Python implementation of the Grey Wolf Algorithm. Technology: Python. Tool: Network simulator. The project was developed and tested as a college project.
